basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Recordatus autem Dominus Noe, cunctorumque animantium, et omnium jumentorum quae erant'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Recordatus autem Dominus Noe, cunctorumque animantium, et omnium jumentorum quae erant cum eo in arca, adduxit spiritum super terram, et imminutae sunt aquae. Potest in nomine Spiritus ipse vivificator Dei Spiritus accipi, de quo in principio dictum est: Et Spiritus Dei ferebatur super aquas (Genes. I, 3), de quo dubium non est quia sicut tunc, congregatis aquis, in locum unum arefecit terram, ita etiam nunc, ablatis de medio aquis diluvii, denuo faciem terrae revelavit. Potest et ventus iste aereus nomine Spiritus appellari, juxta illud Psalmistae: Dixit et stetit spiritus procellae (Psal. CVI, 25), cujus flatibus crebris plerumque solent aquae minui vel de loco moveri; unde est illud Exodi: Cumque extendisset Moyses manum super mare, abstulit illud Dominus, flante vento vehementi et urente tota nocte, et vertit in siccum, divisaque est aqua (Exod. XIV, 27).
